rows.text: The valid limit is 45 days from the employer's request, as set by art. 71, c. 11 of Legislative Decree 81/2008, which the INAIL guide also states. The 60-day term in art. 2, c. 1 of the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 does not match the statute and should not be relied on.

rows.text: When choosing work equipment, the employer must consider four elements listed in Article 71(2)(a) to (d) of Legislative Decree 81/2008: the specific conditions of the work, the risks in the workplace, the risks from using the equipment, and the risks from interference with equipment already in use.

Yes. Under art. 72, c. 2 of D.Lgs. 81/2008, a company renting or lending work equipment without an operator must also obtain and keep on file, for the whole rental or loan period, a self-certification from the renter or borrower (or their employer) confirming that the designated users have received the specific training and instruction required by the Title.

Under Article 71(8), letter c) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 requires that the initial, periodic and extraordinary checks described in letters a) and b) be carried out by a competent person (persona competente).

Mast climbing work platforms (piattaforme di lavoro autosollevanti su colonne) must undergo periodic verification every two years (verifica biennale), per Annex VII, row 10. The INAIL service guide, p. 26, gives the same biennial periodicity.

The passages do not state how long a body's registration in the list under the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 remains valid before renewal. Annex III, points 1 to 3.1 (passage 3) covers the application and the evaluation commission, but the text is cut off before any validity period appears.

rows.text: Under Allegato II, point 3.1.2(a) of DM 11 April 2011, the verifier must examine five documents during the first periodic verification of SC and SP equipment: the EC declaration of conformity, the declaration of correct installation (where required by law), load charts/diagrams (where provided), the work-area diagram (where provided), and the operating instructions. Passage 5 also lists the EC declaration and instructions as documentation examined.

The passages do not say whether a body that issued the CE certification may also carry out the first periodic verification under the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011. Art. 1(1) of the decree only sets its scope, and Annex XI, point 1 of the Machinery Directive bars notified bodies from involvement in the design, construction or marketing of the machines they inspect, but that rule is not stated as applying to DM 2011 verifications.

The scheduled maintenance of chemical fume hoods (cappe chimiche, Art. 16.2 of the Global Service appendix, EN 14175) is semi-annual, so every six months. Filter replacement, which is annual, is excluded from this interval.

Yes. When the manufacturer requests the service and the prototype is examined at its premises, the INAIL suitability recognition extends to the whole series (Guide section 7, p. 43, and section 7.1, p. 44). The manufacturer then issues a certificate of conformity for each unit to the recognized prototype.

rows.value: The RDRL (responsible for the research or teaching activity in the laboratory where the equipment is located), unless the Datore di Lavoro (employer) of the structure indicates otherwise
rows.text: Section 7.3 (Modello C, Registro d'uso della strumentazione) says the RDRL of the laboratory where the equipment is housed decides whether to set up the usage register, unless the employer of the structure (Datore di Lavoro) gives a different instruction.
Under Article 10(7) of the Regulation, if the user requests paper instructions at the time of purchase, the manufacturer must provide them free of charge within one month.

Under Article 13(8) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, importers must keep a copy of the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years after the machinery or related product has been placed on the market.

No. Under Article 15(3) of the Regulation, a distributor that has reason to believe machinery is not in conformity must not make it available on the market until it has been brought into conformity. Informing the manufacturer or importer and the market surveillance authorities is an additional duty where the machinery presents a risk; it does not replace the prohibition.

rows.text: Article 16(1) of Directive 2014/33/EU lists the conformity assessment procedures available for lifts, including a vehicle servicing lift if it is a lift within the Directive. The passages do not classify vehicle servicing lifts separately or state any date-based rule for the 1 March 2027 placing on the market.
Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies in general from 14 January 2027, as set out in Article 54. Articles 26 to 42 and other provisions listed in Article 54 apply from earlier dates.
Under Article 50(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Member States must notify the Commission of the rules on penalties and the implementing measures by 14 October 2026.

No. Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 lets products keep being made available only if they were placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 14 January 2027. A machine first placed on the market on 20 January 2027 falls after that date, so Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 governs it.

Yes. Under Article 10(8) of the Regulation, the manufacturer may provide, instead of the EU declaration of conformity accompanying the machinery, the internet address or machine-readable code where it can be accessed, placed in the instructions for use (see also Annex III, point 1.7.4.2(c)). The digital declaration must remain accessible online for the expected lifetime of the machinery and at least 10 years after placing on the market.

The passages set out the duty in Article 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 to subject Annex VII equipment to periodic verifications, but none of them state a penalty or its amount for failing to do so. The sanctions provisions are not among the passages.

The passages do not state the number of hours. Article 73(5) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 says the duration of the training for operator qualifications, including telescopic handlers, is to be set by the Conferenza permanente per i rapporti tra Stato, le regioni e le province autonome di Trento e di Bolzano, but the specific figure is not given in the provided text.

Passage 0 states that work equipment built without product directives must meet the general safety requirements of Annex V to Legislative Decree 81/2008, but the passages do not set out what Annex V says about emergency stop devices.

The passages do not say which harmonised standard gives presumption of conformity for vehicle servicing lifts under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230. They cover Directive 2014/33 on lifts (Article 14 and recital 18), which is a different instrument, and Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on AI. Passage 5 mentions DIN EN 1493 only as a test reference in a product manual, not as a presumption-of-conformity statement.

The passages do not name Italy's national market surveillance authority for machinery or mention Article 70(4) of Legislative Decree 81/2008. Passage 6 (Machinery Directive, Art. 4(3)) only says Member States must designate competent authorities for machinery conformity.

The crane is a mobile lifting appliance rated above 200 kg used in the extractive sector, so Allegato VII of D.lgs. 81/2008 requires annual verification. The 2010 build year does not change this, because the 10-year age split applies only to other sectors.

value: Verifica annuale, if manufactured more than 10 years before the verification (anno di fabbricazione antecedente 10 anni)
Verifica biennale, if manufactured within the last 10 years (anno di fabbricazione non antecedente 10 anni)
rows.text: The passages do not give the crane's manufacture year, so the frequency cannot be fixed from them. For a mobile lifting device over 200 kg in regular use outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors, the rule is annual verification if it was made more than 10 years earlier and biennial verification if it was made within the last 10 years (Allegato VII, as reflected in passages 8, 9 and 0). The passages also do not say when the last verification occurred, so they cannot confirm what falls due on 31 December 2027.

The passages do not give the last verification date or the manufacturing year for position 13 (IGEA-PRIM 5t overhead travelling crane, table A2 of Allegato A), so the switch from biennial to annual cannot be dated. Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 makes the periodicity depend on the equipment's type, its use in extractive settings, and whether it was built more than 10 years earlier, but the passages do not state which category this crane falls into.

Yes, both have an annual verification interval under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 (table in passage 3): the gantry crane at position 23 (built 1989, Lula) and the PRIM 5t overhead crane (built 1980, Funtana Raminosa) are over 200 kg lifting appliances in the extractive sector, and both were built more than 10 years ago, so the annual rule applies whether they are fixed or mobile. The Tabella B3 entry in passage 4 lists the PRIM crane at position 12, not 13, so the position number in the question may be off.

The passages identify the overhead travelling cranes (gru a ponte scorrevole, positions 8-13 in Table A2) and the gantry crane (gru a cavalletto, position 23 in Table A5) and their mining-area locations, per Igea S.p.A.'s technical sheet. Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 makes fixed lifting equipment over 200 kg in the extractive sector subject to annual verification if it was manufactured more than 10 years ago, and biennial otherwise. The passages do not give the manufacture years or the last verification dates for these units, so it cannot be determined which positions are yearly today.

rows.text: In table A4 (autogru), positions 17, 18 and 21 have a capacity above 5000 kg. Positions 19 and 20 are rated at exactly 5000 kg and position 22 at 2095 kg, so none of those qualifies.

In Table A1 (Allegato A, igea-equipment p. 6), positions 5 and 6 are the only truck-mounted cranes with a capacity below 1000 kg (995 kg each) and a construction year before 2005 (2003 and 2004). Positions 1 to 4 and 7 are excluded because their capacity is 1000 kg or more, their year is 2005 or later, or their capacity is not stated.

The passages do not state how far in advance a periodic verification subsequent to the first must be requested. Article/annex text in the passages gives a 45-day advance-request rule only for the first periodic verification (INAIL guide pp. 29 and 36), and the IGEA contract (p. 4) refers to verifications 'secondo le cadenze ed entro le scadenze previste' without a lead time.

The passages do not say whether moving a GUTTER overhead travelling crane from Masua to another site requires notice to INAIL under the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011. They cover notification duties for other equipment types, and note in the footnote to the sollevamento persone group (p. 35) that for mobile or transferable equipment the competent INAIL office is the one where the equipment is located, but they do not address relocating an overhead crane.

rows.value: The employer (datore di lavoro) bears the cost of the periodic verifications.
rows.text: Under Article 71, paragraph 11 of Legislative Decree 81/2008, the verifications are provided for a fee and their costs are charged to the employer. Passage 4 of the INAIL guide says the same thing: the service carries a cost borne by the user under the tariff set by the 23 November 2012 decree.

The passages do not show point 4.2.2 or identify which section the document list belongs to. Page 5 (passage 3) has a list in which item 4 (manual, CE-marked machines only) does not apply to position 8, and item 5 (structural certification of residual life for equipment over 20 years old) would apply to a 1985 unit, but the list is not confirmed as 4.2.2.
The MA STAR manual says to check the lubrication felt for wear and/or contamination and replace it at least every 12 months (section 7.2.2, Lubricating the Spindle and the Load Nut).
Under section 4.4.4 (Lowering Process) of the MA STAR manual (p. 20), the operator is responsible for ensuring that nobody is within the danger zone before the vehicle is lowered.

The nanoScan3 manual requires the regular thorough checks to be carried out at least once a year, per section 5.6.2 "Planning the regular thorough check" (page 50) and the "Minimum requirements for the regular thorough check" (page 51).

No. Section 18 (Maintenance and Repair), Robot Arm Inspection, of the UR5e manual (p. 210) warns that compressed air can damage the robot arm components and says never to use it to clean the robot arm.
According to the UR5e manual's Long Term Storage guidance (section 17, p. 202), a robot is considered long-term stored when it is stored for 6 months or more.
No. Section 15.1 (Emergency Stop Description, UR10e manual p. 196) says that once an emergency stop is actuated, it must be manually reset at the push-button that initiated the stop.

According to Section 19 (Disposal and Environment) of the UR10e manual, p. 224, the responsibility for disposing of the robot in accordance with applicable national laws, regulations and standards rests with the owner of the robot.

The passages do not identify a DEFRIES-TITANO overhead travelling crane or any position 11, and they do not describe a structural verification certification or residual life cycles for such a crane. Passage 0 gives a design life of 22,000 lifting cycles for a different lift, which is not a residual figure.

The passages set out the periodic verification duty for lifting equipment under Article 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008, but none of them states a penalty for failing to submit a lifting device for verification. The sanction would need to come from a passage not provided.

The passages identify the anchor rod for the MA STAR 3.5 columns as HAS U 5.8 M16 with HILTI HIT HY 200-A adhesive mortar (passage 1, p. 9), but none of them give a tightening torque. The required torque is not stated in the supplied passages.

The passages do not state an MTTFd value. Table 34 in the technical data (passage 1, p. 130) gives PFH = 8 × 10^-8 per hour and a mission time of 20 years for ISO 13849 performance level PL d, but no MTTFd figure.

The passages do not state the weight of the UR5e Control Box. The Control Box dimensions (460 × 449 × 254 mm) are listed in the technical specifications table on p. 16, and the 20.7 kg figure on p. 15 is the robot arm's weight, not the Control Box's. Check the UR5e manual's technical specifications or the product datasheet for the Control Box weight.
